name: Apprenticeship Maryland Program (Youth Apprenticeship)
org: Maryland Department of Labor, Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program

offerings.cycle_label: Ongoing youth apprenticeship across 21 Maryland jurisdictions
offerings.summary: A paid youth apprenticeship where a high schooler works at least 450 hours with a mentor in a high-demand occupation while taking related classes at school.

loc.venue: Participating employer worksites in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico and Worcester Counties and Baltimore City

grades.raw: Presently available to high school students in twenty Maryland counties

school.raw: High school students in participating counties may apply to be a youth apprentice by contacting their school's work-based learning coordinator, their school counselor, or their school system's Youth Apprenticeship Coordinator.

items.raw: Pay the youth apprentice for all work performed during the program at no less than minimum wage

sched.dur_raw: work a minimum of 450 hours within not to exceed 14 months

app.instructions: Contact the school's work-based learning coordinator, school counselor, or the school system's Youth Apprenticeship Coordinator

issues: The FAQ does not state a grade level; grades 11 and 12 are recorded from the programme's structure and flagged for confirmation
Pay is defined as at least minimum wage, which varies by employer
Worksites are assigned by the employer and school system
